title: Panthers Volleyball Ousted From Playoffs
text:
The Medomak Valley volleyball team lost to Wells 3-2 in a competitive Class C quarterfinal match on Saturday, Oct. 24 in Waldoboro. The No. 7 seed Warriors upset the No. 2 seed Panthers in a best-of-five match that went the full distance.
Wells won the first set 26-24. The Panthers bounced back to knot the match by taking the second set 27 25. Medomak took a 2-1 lead when they won the third set 25-17. Wells battled back, winning the fourth set 25-23 to force a fifth and deciding set. The Warriors outlasted the Panthers in the fifth set 15-10.

title: Families hold out hope for loved ones missing after deadly Spain train crash
text:
Families hold out hope for loved ones missing after deadly Spain train crash
Families desperately searched for missing loved ones Thursday, more than 24 hours after two high-speed trains collided in central Spain, killing at least 69 and injuring dozens of others.
“I have my father, and I don’t know where he is. I hope to find him, oh my Lord," said César Vicente, an actor who traveled 495 kilometers (307 miles) from his native Seville to Toledo in search of his father. He spent the night with many other families at a religious center converted into a base for those affected by the disaster.
Vicente was with his mother and his aunt, all of whom were looking for César Vicente, who was sitting in seat 13A on the RENFE train that struck another operated by the private company Iryo, which had stopped on the tracks. The family was among those who braved the cold to take a short walk on a chilly morning.
Related video: Spain train derailment, Jan. 2026
“I don’t want this to happen to anyone. This is unbearable,” he added. “This is hell.”
Online, relatives and friends flooded social media with desperate appeals for information on the whereabouts of their loved ones, posting photos or describing the clothes they were wearing when they boarded the trains bound for Seville and details about their physical appearance or the seat in which they were traveling.
In a post Wednesday on Instagram, Alejandra Marroquín told her followers that her sister Adriana, who was wearing dark blue clothes, was traveling in car 8 of the RENFE train and that they had been unable to contact her.
“We’re still praying, we don’t know anything,” Marroquín said in a post Thursday morning, as search teams with sniffer dogs continued to look for victims.
“The entire government is working to respond to the victims’ families, shed light on the tragedy, and strengthen security so that this never happens again,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez told reporters on Thursday morning.
This was the second high-speed rail disaster this year. In January, 46 people died after one train jumped the track and slammed into the side of another going the opposite way in southern Spain.
The high-speed rail network has been considered one of Spain’s crowning achievements. It is the world’s second-largest, after China’s. Until this year, it had not experienced a deadly crash since coming into service over three decades ago.
The crash set off a wave of solidarity
Life in Urda, a small town of about 2,500 people south of Madrid, was turned upside down early Wednesday.
Residents rushed to help in any way they could: from assisting the injured to preparing sandwiches for the unharmed passengers, many of whom they even carried from the tracks to a nearby sports pavilion in their cars.
David Gómez, a construction worker, was working with his brother and another colleague nearby when they heard the crash and ran to help, he told the newspaper El País.
“People were trying to get out through the windows ... We cut through some fences to access the area and treated people with the first-aid kits we had brought until emergency services arrived," he said.
With 180 people injured, including 110 taken to hospitals, authorities issued a call for blood donations.
The response was immediate: in Castilla-La Mancha alone, the region where the collision occurred, more than 2,000 people volunteered in the aftermath.
“I want to express my personal and very sincere gratitude to everyone who has stepped up, starting with the all-time record number of donations,” said the region’s president, Emiliano García-Page, who also thanked the 1,300 emergency service personnel who were mobilized.
___
Medrano reported from Madrid.

title: Netanyahu, chief rival fall short of parliamentary majority, leaving path to government unclear
text:
Netanyahu, chief rival Eisenkot fall short of parliamentary majority, leaving path to government unclear
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party on Thursday amplified unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance, as final results showed his bloc had lost its majority in parliament.
The opposition accused Netanyahu of demonizing the Arab population after a historic showing by Arab-led parties in an attempt to delegitimize the election. If the rest of the opposition teams up with Arab parties, a rare and politically risky move, they could potentially form a majority government in parliament, the Knesset.
Results released by election officials on Thursday showed Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats in the 120-member assembly, well below the 68 seats it had controlled at its peak in the previous parliament. His main opposition won 48 seats and Arab-led parties secured the other 19.
The count is complete, but the results still need to be certified and submitted to the country's president next Wednesday.
Netanyahu's party, Likud, has been spreading claims of malfeasance by Arab-led parties since exit polls indicated the prime minister had suffered a setback in Tuesday's vote. But it ramped up the rhetoric after the head of Israel's election committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, said that “serious suspicions” of foreign interference had been brought before him.
In a letter to the Shin Bet security agency, Sohlberg said he could not verify the claims. But given their serious nature, he asked the agency to investigate.
Netanyahu's party responded with an inflammatory statement: "The elections in Israel have been stolen!” it said, claiming — without evidence — that the alleged election interference was “aimed at facilitating a foreign takeover of the Knesset, the Islamization of Israel and toppling of the right wing government.”
Israeli media reported that members of Netanyahu’s party were accusing Qatar — a country that many Israelis view as a patron of Hamas, the Gaza-based militant group.
Qatar issued a quick denial, calling the allegations “ridiculous and dangerous.”
As it announced its results early Wednesday, the election commission said the investigation was based on classified intelligence. It did not elaborate but warned of “unfounded” reports surrounding the probe.
“It does not affect the final results that will be submitted to the president, nor does it concern any particular sector of the population,” it said.
Netanyahu's opponents accuse him of undermining vote
Netanyahu's main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, said Likud was trying to delegitimize the results. “They are doing this because they lost,” he said.
Eisenkot ridiculed the accusation of foreign interference with a tongue-in-cheek statement, saying: “I welcome the fact that Netanyahu is finally condemning Qatari involvement in the State of Israel.”
Netanyahu has long faced accusations that former top aides of his accepted money from Qatar.
By casting doubt on the vote, Netanyahu appeared to be positioning himself to block any potential alliance between his opponents and the Arab parties. Netanyahu has suggested that it would be treasonous for Eisenkot to join with Arab parties.
The projected outcome of the results was expected to show both Netanyahu's bloc of religious and nationalist allies and his more secular and socially liberal opponents falling short of a parliamentary majority required to form a new government. The Arab parties would hold the remaining seats and could potentially give Eisenkot the backing he needs to oust Netanyahu.
The Shin Bet, seeking to calm tensions, said its investigation was not meant to “cast aspersions” on an entire section of the population that "exercised its right to vote in a democratic and lawful manner.”
The elections committee also sounded a note of caution in a letter written to a concerned member of parliament. It said that even though an investigation was taking place, “allegations of systematic violations of electoral integrity are baseless.”
The committee wants findings from the Shin Bet within the week. Israeli law requires election results to be certified by Nov. 4.
Netanyahu campaigned on anti-Arab sentiment
Even ahead of the vote, Netanyahu and Likud painted the Arab-led parties as a danger to Israel, which critics called an attempt to further marginalize Arab citizens. Arab citizens of Palestinian descent make up 20% of the population but are often viewed with suspicion because of their sympathies with other Palestinians.
Those campaign attacks, along with anger over the divisive Netanyahu and his far-right government, brought outraged Arabs to the polls like never before.
On Thursday, Yair Golan, head of the Democrats party, accused Netanyahu of “attempting to undermine the election results through an ugly delegitimization campaign directed against the will of the public — and against the Arab public in particular.”
“Netanyahu is working to steal the election,” the Arab-led Joint List party asserted Thursday.
The head of the Arab-led Ra’am party, Mansour Abbas, welcomed the investigation into election interference and said his party had nothing to do with the case, while accusing Netanyahu of a campaign of incitement.
President Isaac Herzog called it a “sensitive moment” and called for a full investigation. He warned that “we must not tarnish an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy.”
Difficult decisions are ahead as parties seek coalitions
The developments amplified the difficult decisions for the weeks ahead. Those include whether some Jewish and Arab parties would team up in a historic alliance, or whether some parties that campaigned on ousting Netanyahu would toss that aside and join forces with him.
While the race for a 61-seat majority needed to control the 120-seat Knesset plays out, Netanyahu remains in charge.
If Netanyahu loses office, that would set off a cascade of events that critics say he has desperately sought to avoid. He would be taken to account over yearslong corruption allegations, and an inquiry almost certainly would begin into the security failures that led to the devastating Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attack.
Eisenkot has left door open to cooperation with Arab-led parties
Even without a role in a coalition, Arab-led parties could assert their growing power by supporting other Netanyahu opponents in the next parliament. That could include electing a new speaker, giving them control of the agenda and potentially allowing them to advance and pass legislation before a new government is formed.
Eisenkot has indicated he is open, with conditions, to joining forces with the Arab-led parties. Ahmad Tibi, second on the Arab-led Joint List, told Army Radio the opposition bloc reached out to him to discuss replacing the Knesset speaker, and he told them the party would support the bloc’s candidate.
There were small rallies overnight in Tel Aviv, and in far more conservative Jerusalem, in support of a coalition that includes Arab-led parties. Until 2021, no Arab party had joined a coalition government, and that was brief.
If a new government cannot be formed after multiple attempts, Israel would face a new election early next year. On Wednesday, Herzog signaled he wanted to avoid that step – something Eisenkot has said as well.
New elections bring new questions, including whether Arab citizens would again go to the polls in large numbers and whether the tens of thousands of Israelis who flew home to vote would do it again. Many had said they took that step to save the country from Netanyahu.
___
Saeed reported from Abu Snan, Israel. Associated Press reporters across Israel contributed.

title: 'Is this what I think it is?": TSA officers recover wolverine-like claws in airport carry-on
text:
Claw-some catch: TSA officers recover wolverine-like claws in airport carry-on
"Is this what I think this is?" That's what two Transportation Security Administration officers asked themselves after discovering an unusual object inside an airport carry-on bag.
TSA said officers Douglas Linn and Dennis Oishi "teamed up together to identify, confirm and stop a dangerous item in a carry-on bag," which was said to resemble a mix between wolverine-style claws and Freddy Krueger blades.
"A sharp reminder that some accessories are better suited for movie screens than airplane cabins," TSA said about the object.
Related video: Fossilized eggs reveal new secrets about world’s biggest dinosaurs
The item was found during X-ray imaging at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. The bag was then immediately searched.
“I saw three blades and distinct claw-like features,” Linn said. “I was amazed, and even more so when it came out of the bag. I have never seen anything like this during my two years at TSA.”
TSA said the passenger immediately remembered the items after Oishi removed them from the bag and voluntarily abandoned them at the checkpoint.

title: Hackers claim leak of sensitive details on thousands of DHS workers
text:
Hackers claim leak of sensitive details on thousands of DHS workers
The Department of Homeland Security is investigating after hackers claimed to have stolen and leaked the sensitive personal information of tens of thousands of current and former department employees, including some that work on covert and sensitive missions.
"DHS is aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively," a department spokesperson told CNN. "We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected."
A source familiar with the data breach confirmed that the information of some undercover personnel had been exposed.
A hacktivist group calling itself the Department of Peace obtained the data, and the anti-secrecy group Distributed Denial of Secrets posted it online on Wednesday, according to a statement from the latter group.
The group's co-founder, Emma Best, said that the leak "identifies many of the architects and drivers of DHS policy and operations."
A preliminary CNN review of the data found that at least some of the personal information attributed to DHS personnel in the leak is accurate. The data includes phone numbers, work supervisors and assignments for DHS personnel.
Also in the breach is data belonging to at least three Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol officers who were involved in shootings during the second Trump administration, according to the CNN review.
U.S. officials familiar with the data leak reacted with a mix of concern and grim familiarity. One official called the leak "embarrassing," but added "we have certainly seen worse." They expressed concern about the possibility of phishing and doxxing stemming from the data dump.
The data was taken from an "internal" DHS database linked with a "single sign-on service" used by employees, according to Distributed Denial of Secrets.
DHS reiterated to its workforce Thursday that they were aware of the alleged data breach, according to an internal memo reviewed by CNN, adding that they're "working to understand the scope of the situation, assess potential threats, and identify appropriate resources and protective measures." In an earlier memo, employees were also pointed to previously shared resources offered to personnel for removing personally identifiable information from the internet.
The leak "reveals information that can be used by hackers to target the computers and devices of DHS personnel engaged in sensitive investigations and security work," said Thomas Warrick, a former deputy assistant secretary for counterterrorism policy at DHS. He called for a thorough investigation from Congress of how the breach occurred.
"DHS can't just lock the barn door after the horse was stolen," Warrick added. "It needs to make sure DHS and its contractors focus more on keeping the barn locked."
"This hack has just served to put thousands of ordinary civil servants in the crosshairs of anonymous internet trolls," said Sarah Pierce, director of social policy at the Third Way think tank, and a former official at DHS's US Citizenship and Immigration Services agency.
"Many of these employees have served the federal government for decades, under multiple administrations," Pierce told CNN. "They didn't design these policies, and they don't deserve to be punished for them."
It's just latest example of U.S. law enforcement agencies scrambling to respond to their agents' data being posted online. Last month, the FBI was dealing with its most serious breach in years after a cybercriminal group called ShinyHunters claimed to access data on thousands of current and former FBI personnel.
That data heist included information on FBI personnel working in sensitive units focused on China and Russia, according to sources who have seen the data.

title: Letters to the Editor: A better slogan
Best friends become rivals during World Series
text:
'Once in a lifetime': Best friends become rivals during World Series
Two best friends have become temporary rivals as their MLB teams face each other in the World Series.
Brittany Anair and Clare Bartel are best friends the majority of the time, but this week specifically, they're on opposite sides.
Anair has been a Tampa Bay Rays fan since 1998, when the team played its first game. Bartel is a lifelong Milwaukee Brewers fan.
The two women celebrated Anair's 40th birthday at a Rays vs. Brewers game in Milwaukee back in April, when they began dreaming of a World Series matchup between their two teams.
Video below: Sun, sand and a shot at a title: Brewers fans enjoy Florida ahead of Game 5
As it started to look like it could be a possibility, Bartel bought tickets to Game 4 before either team had even clinched a spot yet.
Bartel flew in from Montana Tuesday morning to watch this game with Anair.
They're both hoping their team comes out on top, although things aren't looking like they'll go the Rays' way.
The women said there is something special about sharing this moment.
"It's once in a lifetime," Anair said.
"Especially for us," Bartel added.
"It's like once in a lifetime for our two teams to be here and to be together and to get to celebrate together and just have so much fun together," Anair said. "I'm so excited, and we wouldn't trade that for the world."
They've been showing off their team gear and enjoying some friendly trash talk. They say they're just happy to experience it together.

title: Leita Jackson (1935-2026)
Interfaith Council to host Community Sing
text:
BRUNSWICK, ME – The Brunswick Area Interfaith Council will host We the People SING: All Voices Matter – A Pre-election Community Sing on Sunday Nov. 1 at 3:30 pm at the Gazebo on the Brunswick Mall.
Songs and readings will highlight the promise of our democracy and of our multi faith nation – that everyone participates and that all are valued. Participants are invited to bring a light (candle, lantern…) to use as darkness falls on the first day of daylight saving time.
Familiar and some new easy to learn songs will be shared by a diverse group of song leaders, and lyric sheets will be provided. These are songs for all voices and designed to connect, inspire and unite us in the days just before the election.
One of the song leaders, Rev. Kharma Amos of the Unitarian Universalist Church of Brunswick, shares “As we approach the election, we gather in community because we need one another–all of us. Singing together helps us connect with our bodies and with the ever-richer harmonies that emerge when we each simply sing our part. This gathering is not designed for professional voices, nor is it intended to be a polished performance; rather, it is an invitation to be real and rooted in the knowledge that every voice in our democracy matters. Our songs of love and unity testify to a reality many of our spiritual traditions still believe is possible, and we make it more so when we work for it together.”
Participants are also invited to bring a chair if needed for this free gathering, and hot chocolate will be served.
The Brunswick Area Interfaith Council (BAIC) is a non-sectarian, non-profit organization committed to fostering understanding, respect and cooperation among diverse faith traditions in the Brunswick area. Through collaborative efforts, BAIC promotes the spiritual, moral and social welfare of the larger Brunswick area community.

title: Border Patrol agent charged with murder in wife’s death
text:
LAREDO, Texas (KGNS/Gray News) — A U.S. Border Patrol agent in Texas has been charged in connection with the death of his wife.
Abel Garza, 30, has been charged with murder, a first-degree felony, in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, after a domestic disturbance in south Laredo.
U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed in a statement that Garza is a Border Patrol agent.
Garza also is charged with two counts of endangering a child and two counts of abandonment of a child. All four counts are second-degree felonies.
He was transported to Webb County Jail, and his bond was set at $1 million.
What police say happened
The incident happened just before 3 a.m. Wednesday at a home near Texana Street and Nocona Street.
Chief Miguel Rodriguez said police were initially called about a man knocking on doors asking for help. A police drone spotted a car leaving as officers arrived. Officers stopped the car and found Landeros in the back floorboard with critical stab wounds.
Landeros died later at the hospital. Her death marks Laredo’s sixth homicide of 2026.
Driver detained, children found safe
The 30-year-old driver, later identified as Garza, was detained. Police said the two were a couple. Officers found two children safe at the home.
“The person is in LPD custody, but they’re still in the process of formulating charges with the District Attorney’s Office guiding us,” Joe Baeza, of the Laredo Police Department, said.
CBP statement
In a statement, U.S. Customs and Border Protection said the man is an off-duty Laredo Sector agent who was arrested at 6 a.m. The agency said its Office of Professional Responsibility is reviewing the case.

title: FIRST ALERT WEATHER: Temperatures soar into the 60s Thursday before cooler weather returns this weekend
text:
PRESQUE ISLE, Maine (WAGM) - Good evening everyone and happy Wednesday. We’ve had another fairly quiet day across the region today, with high pressure continuing to influence our weather. Some changes are on the way heading into tomorrow though, with a change in wind direction helping to push temperatures well above average for this time of year. Unfortunately, the warmer weather won’t stick around for too long, as another cold front is expected to bring temperatures back down heading into the upcoming weekend. The other unfortunate part of the forecast is that we’re still not looking at any sort of substantial rainfall to help improve our ongoing drought conditions.
Skies are expected to remain mostly clear to partly cloudy through the rest of tonight. Temperatures won’t be quite as cold as what we experienced last night, but we’re still looking at another chilly night across the region. Low temperatures for most locations will fall back into the upper 20s to lower 30s, with some of our colder locations in southern Aroostook County falling into the mid 20s. A light southwesterly wind will help prevent temperatures from falling quite as far as they did last night, as warmer air begins to work its way into the region.
Tomorrow is shaping up to be a pretty nice day across the region, especially considering we’re just a few days away from the start of November. We’ll start the morning off with plenty of sunshine, with some additional cloud coverage possible as we work our way into the afternoon hours. I don’t expect the additional clouds to ruin the day by any means, especially with temperatures expected to climb well into the 60s by the afternoon. Winds will be coming from the southwest tomorrow, generally around 5 to 10 MPH, with some gusts approaching 20 to 25 MPH during the afternoon hours. Rain chances remain pretty minimal throughout the day, so I wouldn’t be too concerned about any sort of wet weather ruining your outdoor plans.
The real highlight of tomorrow’s forecast will be the temperatures. With high pressure shifting east of the region, we’ll begin to see more of a southwesterly flow develop, helping to bring much warmer air into Aroostook County. High temperatures are expected to climb into the lower to mid 60s for most locations, with a few of our warmer towns potentially reaching the mid 60s. For some perspective, Caribou’s average high temperature for tomorrow is only 48 degrees, meaning we’re looking at temperatures running around 15 to 16 degrees above average. Not too bad for the end of October, especially after starting off this week with temperatures struggling to get out of the lower 40s!
Unfortunately, the warmer temperatures won’t last forever. Looking at our weather setup across the country this evening, you’ll notice a developing storm system across the Upper Midwest, with a cold front extending southward from the system. This is the next weather system we’ll be watching as it moves eastward over the next couple of days. Showers are possible across northern and western portions of Aroostook County Thursday night, with additional shower activity possible across the rest of the region heading into Friday. I don’t expect this to be a particularly impressive rainmaker for us though. The latest forecast guidance continues to suggest that this cold front will be lacking the moisture needed to produce substantial rainfall, with most locations likely seeing less than a tenth of an inch. Some towns may end up seeing little to no measurable rainfall at all.
The lack of substantial rainfall continues to be a major concern considering the ongoing drought across the region. According to the National Weather Service in Caribou, 58 percent of their forecast area is currently experiencing severe drought conditions. Streamflow levels also remain exceptionally low, with 26 of the 38 monitored USGS stream gauges across the region reporting flows much below normal. Unfortunately, I don’t see much in the forecast over the next several days that’s going to make a meaningful difference in those conditions.
For more details on what to expect heading into the end of the work week and the upcoming weekend, make sure to check out my First Alert Video Forecast attached to this article. Have a great evening!

title: Two men accused of sexually assaulting five Maine girls, ages 12 to 14
text:
Two men accused of sexually assaulting five Maine girls, ages 12 to 14
Two men have been indicted by an Oxford County Grand Jury on charges alleging the sexual assault of five girls between the ages of 12 and 14 in Rumford earlier this year.
On Aug. 3, Rumford police started investigating reports of a possible sexual assault involving a minor at the Swainbrook Apartments on Spruce Street. As police looked into the reports, they learned that five girls were involved.
Police say the girls met an adult man from Rumford who they did not previously know and went with him to an apartment at Swainbrook and joined a gathering with that man and another man they did not know.
Police say the men gave the girls alcohol and marijuana and engaged in sexual acts with the girls.
Following an extensive investigation, including interviews with witnesses, evidence was presented to a grand jury on Oct. 14.
Diego Ramirez, 29, who lives in the Swainbrook Apartments, was charged with four counts of gross sexual assault, one count of sexual abuse of a minor, three counts of unlawful sexual contact (two felony, one misdemeanor), aggravated unlawful furnishing of scheduled drugs, endangering the welfare of a child, furnishing liquor to a minor, and allowing a minor to possess or consume alcohol.
Ramirez was initially arrested by Rumford Police on Aug. 9 and charged with preliminary felony sexual offenses and child endangerment in connection with the investigation. Following his arrest, he was released on bail pending further court proceedings and presentation of the case to the grand jury.
Ramirez was then arrested at about 7:10 a.m. on Tuesday after someone called 911 to report a possibly unresponsive man in a vehicle at the intersection of Darnit Road and Brock School Road in Buckfield.
When a deputy from the Oxford County Sheriff's Office arrived, they found Ramirez in the car, said he was not in crisis or having any medical emergency, and then learned he was wanted.
Nkialuzitu Mayingi, 31, of Preble Street in Gorham was indicted on five counts of gross sexual assault, four counts of unlawful sexual contact, aggravated unlawful furnishing of scheduled drugs, endangering the welfare of a child, and furnishing liquor to a minor.
Police were initially unable to locate Mayingi. On Sept. 16, he was found and arrested in Cumberland County and then taken to the Oxford County Jail, where he remained in custody, unable to post bail, when the grand jury returned the indictments on Oct. 14.
"The allegations in this case are deeply disturbing. Five young girls, ranging in age from just 12 to 14, were allegedly provided alcohol and drugs and subjected to serious sexual assaults by adults," said Rumford Police Chief Tony Milligan. "Protecting children from sexual abuse and assault is among our highest responsibilities, and we take that responsibility very seriously. This case also serves as an important reminder to parents, teenagers, and younger children about personal safety and the dangers of placing their trust in people they do not know. Accepting rides from strangers, accompanying unfamiliar adults to private residences, or going places without a parent's knowledge or approval can expose young people to serious risks. What may initially seem like an innocent or harmless situation can quickly become something very different. Young people are naturally curious, increasingly independent, and sometimes more confident in their ability to recognize danger than their life experience might justify. That's part of growing up. But the world can be a dangerous place, and not everyone they encounter has good intentions. It's our responsibility as parents, guardians, and adults to help them understand those realities before they find themselves in a situation they are unprepared to handle."
Milligan also stressed that the responsibility for the alleged assaults rests solely on the men accused of committing the crimes, not on the children.

title: Antidepressants: What to know before you decide
text:
(Aging Untold) — Feeling low, disconnected or not like yourself for weeks or months is different from a bad day. When it starts to affect sleep, energy or everyday life, it’s time to talk about support and treatment options. For some people, that could include an antidepressant.
Start with a conversation with your provider
Dr. Rhea Rogers, a board-certified physician, said the decision looks different for everyone.
“Everybody is individualized so you can just talk with your provider,” Rogers said.
Rogers said to recognize whether you’re feeling depressed and to look at signs such as loss of sleep, loss of energy or loss of motivation.
Some people might also experience a triggering event that starts a downward spiral, which they can’t pull themself out of, she said.
“When your quality of life is being affected, then you might want to look into antidepressant therapy,” Rogers said.
Antidepressants are not “happy pills”
Rogers cautioned that antidepressants do not take away sadness.
She listed chronic stress, a thyroid imbalance and nutritional deficiencies as examples of what could be going on.
Gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck said medication doesn’t change the circumstance.
“What they’ll do is they’ll change the chemical imbalance in the brain to help you get to a place to be better,” Cradduck said. “But you can’t just take a pill and be done.”
She said talk therapy is part of the process. The conversation does not have to be with a therapist, she said, but it needs to address the issues that led to the low mood.
“You need to be willing to face that, or it’s just going to continue in a cycle,” Cradduck said.
Ask about the drug, the dose and the withdrawal symptoms
Aging expert Amy O’Rourke recommended a good psychiatrist and a thorough assessment.
Those who decide to take an antidepressant should get help deciding which one as well as the dose, then track how it’s affecting you, she said.
Aging expert Amy O’Rourke recommended finding a good psychiatrist and getting a thorough assessment to help you decide whether to take an antidepressant, which one and at what dose. She also recommended tracking how it’s affecting you.
She described a client who was prescribed an antidepressant and felt like she was having a panic attack, with a racing heartbeat and sweating. The client called her psychiatrist, who took her off the medication and prescribed a different one.
O’Rourke said she’d want to know the withdrawal symptoms before someone starts taking an antidepressant.
Rogers said there are a lot of withdrawal symptoms.
“You cannot just stop it all of a sudden,” she said.
Rogers said people do not all respond to the same drugs. She said if you can afford it, finding out your genetic variations is one investment worth making, because it can help you respond better to your situation.
Look for support beyond medication
Aging well coach Katherine Ambrose mentioned talk therapy, journaling and filling your mind with as much positivity as possible along with seeking support from medical professionals.
“Don’t forget about things like your thyroid, or your hormones or your nutrients,” Rogers added.
“Talk to your doctors, seek answers, get your rebound and come back,” Ambrose said. “Try everything you can because it’s worth bringing yourself back.”
Rogers said it does not have to be one isolated thing that brought you to this point.

title: NASA astronauts conduct 100th US spacewalk outside International Space Station
text:
NASA astronauts conduct 100th US spacewalk outside International Space Station
NASA astronauts made history on Thursday as they conducted the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the International Space Station.
NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk exited the station to install and deploy a new roll-out solar array on the station's port-side truss.
NASA said the additional power will help support critical station operations, including its eventual safe and controlled deorbit.
The next spacewalk is scheduled for Nov. 5 to install the eighth and final roll-out solar array.

title: NFL Week 8 schedule, predictions and more
text:
NFL Week 8 schedule, predictions and more
NFL Week 8 schedule, predictions and more
The calendar is turning to a new month, and as we're approaching the halfway point of the 2026 season, it's also time for NFL trade deadline preparations to begin.
Video above: Boston researchers share new estimate of CTE in ex-NFL players
With many teams still very much in the playoff picture, and others looking to retool for next year and beyond, some big changes could be on the horizon.
For now, it's time to settle in and enjoy some good games this weekend. For the first time since Week 3, all games will be played on U.S. soil. Last week featured the first NFL game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints.
Next week, Madrid, Spain, hosts a game for the second year in a row.
Here's a look at what's ahead this week, as Matthew Peaslee of the Hearst National Team continues his predictions. Peaslee went 10-4 in his Week 6 predictions and sits at 63-43-1 on the year.
All game times are in Eastern Standard Time.
Thursday, Oct. 29
Carolina Panthers (3-3) vs. Green Bay Packers (4-3), 8:15 p.m.
The Packers had a crazy game against the Lions, but lost too many bad breaks down the stretch. They should be able to bounce back this week back home at Lambeau Field. Josh Jacobs was back in action last week and reformed the Packers offense. But this game will be won in the trenches, and if the Green Bay defense can rattle Bryce Young, it'll be a solid evening to start the weekend.
Prediction: Packers 28, Panthers 23
Sunday, Nov. 1
Baltimore Ravens (4-3) vs. Buffalo Bills (5-1), 1 p.m.
The Bills are surrendering 28.5 points per game, which is the third-most in the NFL. Yet, they're still 5-1 and in prime position to win their division. The offense is just that good and will continue to roll this week. Buffalo averages 387.7 yards per game with 148 rushing yards per game. Josh Allen is the centerpiece of the offense, but without James Cook III, the Bills wouldn't be as powerful as they have been this year.
Prediction: Bills 28, Ravens 21
Tennessee Titans (1-6) vs. Cincinnati Bengals (4-2), 1 p.m.
The Titans might not be as bad as their record suggests. Things are starting to come together and Robert Selah's head coaching position may be salvaged, especially if an upset can be pulled in Cincinnati. The Titans' defense is suspect, but Anthony Hill Jr. is among the league leaders in tackles with 68 and Jeffery Simmons does a good job getting to the quarterback, so Joe Burrow better watch out. The offense did enough last week to win, but suffered a heartbreaking three-point loss to Cleveland. Tennessee did find a key cog in Tony Pollard, who had a 129-yard, three-touchdown performance. It's certainly bold, but a Titans win would be beautiful in an otherwise ugly season.
Prediction: Titans 26, Bengals 18
Arizona Cardinals (2-5) vs. Dallas Cowboys (3-4), 1 p.m.
Things are getting brighter for the Dallas Cowboys. Dak Prescott will likely surpass 2,000 passing yards for the season after this one is finished — and the Cowboys should be celebrating a big win. If Prescott can find CeeDee Lamb for at least two touchdowns, and Javonte Williams continues his powerful displays on the ground, it could be a blowout. For the Cardinals, Jacoby Brissett and Trey McBride are a solid pitch-and-catch combination too.
Prediction: Cowboys 28, Cardinals 7
Minnesota Vikings (6-0) vs. Detroit Lions (4-2), 1 p.m.
The Vikings defense has spearheaded their way to an unblemished record. Dallas Turner is among the league leaders in sacks with six and Byron Murphy Jr. has three interceptions. But the streak may come to an end this week. The Lions pulled off a gritty win over the rival Packers last week and have the momentum remaining at home. Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown are turning into a three-headed monster in Detroit.

Four weeks ago, the Browns and Steelers played a tight match in Cleveland and now as it turns to Pittsburgh, the division title could be on the line. The Steelers come in winners of three straight and have the veteran leadership of Aaron Rodgers, who is playing as confidently as at any point in his 22 seasons. The Dolphins finally picked up a win last week. The same can't be said for the Chargers this week. The Raiders have an outside chance at winning the division, but these two teams are still the class of the AFC West. title: Economist explains how the ‘K-shaped economy’ is impacting the midterms
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail.
“Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. How that pie is distributed affects how a large segment of the population and the voters are feeling about the economy right now.”
The contradiction has been described by many economists recently, as the “k-shaped” economy, using a graph to depict how high-income earners and asset owners are doing compared to middle and lower-income earners.
“To be concrete, the wealthiest households are presumed to spend much more than the lowest ones, not only in absolute terms, which is obvious, but also as a share of their income and in their wealth,” Rebucci said.
In recent months on the campaign trail, President Donald Trump has said that the U.S. economy is doing well, often conflicting with what recent consumer surveys have found on voters’ economic opinions.
“The economy is the greatest economy we’ve ever had, by far,” said Trump, at an Aug. 5 rally in Las Vegas.
The trend is not unusual. Each election cycle, the party in power in Washington typically proclaims that the U.S. economy is strong.
Despite the stark differences that voters appear to be thinking about this election season, Rebucci said Americans have long lived with inequality in the economy.
“This is an economy that is comfortable with inequality,” he said. “The issue is not about eliminating the inequality, but to adjust the system in such a way that we can live better with that inequality. And in particular, the most important thing that people need to be perceiving is that they’ve got a shot at being in that top 10%, top 1%.”

title: Maine State Police arrest Milford man in infant daughter's death
text:
Maine State Police arrest Milford man in infant daughter's death
Maine State Police have arrested a Milford man in connection with the death of his 13-month-old daughter, who died of hypothermia shortly after Christmas last year.
Maine State Police arrest Milford man in infant daughter's death
Maine State Police have arrested a Milford man in connection with the death of his 13-month-old daughter, who died of hypothermia shortly after Christmas last year.
Maine State Police announced the arrest of a 37-year-old Milford man Wednesday in connection with the death of his 13-month-old daughter, whose body was found in Milford shortly after Christmas last year.
Shane McLaughlin was charged with manslaughter and three counts of endangering the welfare of a child, according to state police. The investigation began after Eleanora Ray McLaughlin died on Dec. 28, 2025. An autopsy from the state medical examiner determined her cause of death was hypothermia and initially ruled her death an accident.
McLaughlin was booked at the Penobscot County Jail. He is expected to make an initial court appearance in Bangor, although it's not clear when. The Maine Attorney General's Office is prosecuting the case.
In January, the child's mother, Erika McLaughlin, who lives in West Virginia now, told Maine's Total Coverage that her estranged husband was raising their 2-year-old son and 1-year-old twin daughters in Maine.
Family members confirmed to Maine's Total Coverage on Thursday that the remaining children are now in the custody of their grandmother, Erika McLaughlin's mother.
Erika McLaughlin said she was told by state officials that her daughter was found in bed, covered in urine. She also said there were multiple Maine Department of Health and Human Services investigations regarding her children.
In January, she said the most recent investigation was specifically regarding her twin 1-year-old daughters. That case was closed on Dec. 22, six days before Eleanora's death.

title: Maine files lawsuit, accusing Trump administration of enabling fraud and corruption
also_topics: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
Maine files lawsuit, accusing Trump administration of enabling fraud and corruption
Maine is one of 20 states, plus the District of Columbia, to sue the Trump administration, trying to stop the gutting of the Corporate Transparency Act (CTA), which helps police and prosecutors catch money launderers, fraudsters, and tax cheats.
"It is inexplicable that the Trump Administration wants to change the rules to make it harder to catch and prosecute white-collar crime," said Maine Attorney General Aaron Frey. "The bipartisan law the Administration is trying to dismantle is an effective mechanism for law enforcement to uncover illegal financial schemes and hold wrongdoers accountable. The American people deserve a system where people and corporations are accountable to the law."
The CTA was enacted into law on January 1, 2021, when the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives voted to override President Donald Trump's veto of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2021.
The law requires corporations, LLCs, and similar entities to report identifying information about their beneficial owners to the United States Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and is designed to stop shell companies from hiding their financial transactions from law enforcement. The law created a Treasury database of business owners to help law enforcement to trace dirty money, track down stolen assets, and uncover bribes and political payoffs.
On March 26, 2025, FinCEN issued a rule which exempted 99.9% of businesses from the law's reporting requirements, which Frey says makes the law nearly useless. Then, on August 14, 2026, FinCEN issued a final rule making these exemptions permanent. When announcing the final rule, FinCEN committed to executing a data purge and deleting all information previously reported by U.S. companies and individuals that are no longer required to report by February 10, 2027.
The lawsuit alleges those actions are violations of the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), the Separation of Powers, and Take Care Clause of the U.S. Constitution. The states seek a court order that vacates FinCEN's new rule and declares it unlawful. Furthermore, the Complaint seeks a court order enjoining FinCEN from implementing or effectuating the data purge.
The other states to join the lawsuit are Arizona, California, Colorado, Delaware, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Rhode Island, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, as well as the District of Columbia.

title: Hornbill receives 3D-printed beak, marking historic first
text:
Hornbill receives 3D-printed beak, marking historic first
An injured hornbill now has a new custom-made beak, marking a historic first.
The southern hornbill at the ARTIS Royal Zoo in Amsterdam has received what veterinarians say is the first known 3D-printed model to replace both the upper and lower parts of a bird’s beak.
The bird broke both parts of his beak and was left with stumps. He could still manage, but had trouble picking up food from the ground and grooming his feathers, his caretakers said.
Veterinarians and bird specialists worked with Utrecht University’s Faculty of Veterinary Medicine to develop a solution.
Specialists used a CT scan of the hornbill’s head and the broken pieces of his original beak to design the prosthesis. The beak parts were printed in plastic and attached with titanium components and screws.
The devices can be removed if necessary.
The hornbill began using his new beak the afternoon after surgery. By the next morning, zoo officials say he was picking up a mouse from the ground and eating on his own.
He is still practicing and adjusting to the beak’s shape and added weight, zoo staffers said, adding they will closely monitor his recovery and behavior.
Veterinarians said they hope the beak will help him resume natural behaviors, including feeding and grooming, and support interaction with his mate. They also hope the pair may have offspring in the future.
The team says the procedure could offer lessons for treating other birds, though beak shape and anatomy vary by species.

title: 2 college students found dead after going missing during Colorado hike
text:
Two Colorado college students have been found dead after going missing during a hiking trip in the Rocky Mountains last weekend when a heavy snowstorm hit, authorities said.
The bodies of Kaden Matsuda, 19, of Ridgway, Colorado, and Jackson Donlon, 20, of New York, were found Wednesday afternoon in a basin of West Apostle Mountain, about 100 miles (160 kilometers) southeast of Aspen, the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement posted on social media.
They left Colorado Mountain College Leadville’s campus on Friday, telling family and friends they planned to hike up Ice Mountain, a nearly 14,000-foot (4,270-meter) peak near West Apostle Mountain that requires technical climbing, the sheriff’s office said. They were expected back by Sunday, but college staff reported them missing on Monday morning.
The sheriff’s office said the causes of their deaths were under investigation, but foul play was not suspected. Authorities said they would not offer theories on what may have happened until autopsies are completed.
“Our heart aches for Kaden and Jackson’s family and friends,” Sheriff Andy Rohrich said in the statement Wednesday night. “We are very proud of our team’s efforts to find them before this weekend’s coming storm. Although this is a gut punch, our prayers were answered that we would find Kaden and Jackson, allowing some closure for the family.”
About 60 search and rescue volunteers, aided by helicopters, drones and dogs, searched for the two men.
The helicopter crew on Tuesday discovered a tent collapsed under the snow with their sleeping bags, a stove and clothing near a lake northwest of Ice Mountain — but the students were nowhere to be found.
Based on the tent’s location, officials said they were aiming for the 13,597-foot (4,144-meter) West Apostle Mountain.
Friends and family described both as experienced hikers and climbers.
The sheriff’s office said their climbing equipment was not in their dorms, tent or vehicle, suggesting they left their tent prepared for a technical climb. Trash inside the tent indicated they had eaten before starting their hike, officials said.
Matsuda was studying to become a wildland firefighter, and Donlon was studying to become a mountain guide, Rohrich said.
Authorities had been concerned that aerial searches could be limited in upcoming days because of poor weather that was expected to begin Friday.
___
Yu reported from Phoenix. Associated Press writer Dave Collins in Hartford, Connecticut, contributed.

title: Binance reports 'potential security issue' as stablecoin issuers freeze millions in funds
text:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it’s investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident “does look like a hack on Binance.”
It wasn’t immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to accomplish and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered, but stablecoin issuers quickly froze funds Thursday evening.
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement.
“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement continued.
Stablecoin providers Tether and Circle each said they froze funds Thursday in response to the incident.
Jeremy Allaire, co-founder and CEO of Circle, wrote on X that the company had frozen the equivalent of more than $800 million in currency associated with the incident “in coordination with law enforcement.” Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X that the company froze the equivalent of more than $1.5 billion in currency related to “a potential Binance exchange hack.”
The price of bitcoin dropped 3.2% Thursday evening to under $79,000.
Binance was founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao, who in 2023 pleaded guilty to a felony related to his failure to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as CEO. President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.
Zhao posted on X on Thursday that “User funds are safe!” but added that the incident “does look like a hack on Binance.” He added that while he doesn’t manage Binance anymore, “as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”
Zhao was released from prison last year after being sentenced for violating the Bank Secrecy Act. He was the first person ever sentenced to prison time for such violations of that law, which requires U.S. financial institutions to know who their customers are, to monitor transactions and to file reports of suspicious activity. Prosecutors said no one had ever violated the regulations to the extent Zhao did. Zhao and Binance have been key supporters of some of the Trump family’s crypto enterprises.
———
AP Technology Writer Barbara Ortutay contributed.

title: When will we know 2026 midterm election results? It may take some time, but that’s normal
text:
When will we know 2026 midterm election results? It may take some time, but that’s normal
If you go to bed on election night and don’t know who won a midterm congressional race, that’s normal. And if you wake up the next morning and find that a candidate who was behind hours earlier has since pulled ahead, that’s normal, too.
This story was originally published on PolitiFact.com.
That won’t stop some politicians and their allies from spreading misinformation during vote counting.
In past elections, elected leaders, candidates and social media users have spread falsehoods that “late night” arrivals of “ballot dumps” or “suitcases” of ballots are signs of fraud, or that only Democratic-led cities take days to count votes.
Some states such as Florida often complete the majority of their unofficial counts in fewer hours or days than elsewhere. But it is not a sign of fraud if other places need more time.
“States are neither fast or slow, they all count and certify the results in accordance with the laws passed by their state legislature,” said Ryan Macias, an election technology and cybersecurity expert. “What is fast or slow is how quickly the media can collect sufficient evidence to confidently predict the winner, which is typically based on the margin of victory.”
Voters can help elections run smoothly. People who vote by mail, for instance, should not wait until the last minute to submit their ballots. Many election offices provide secure drop boxes to speed the return of mailed ballots. The U.S. Postal Service recommends that voters mail in their ballot at least one week before the deadline.
“There are always a handful of really close Senate and House races in which the winner will not be determined for several days or, in the cases of Alaska and California, as much as a week or two,” said Joe Lenski, executive vice president of SSRS, which conducts a national exit poll on Election Day.
Control of the U.S. Senate could come down to a handful of close races with large numbers of ballots to count.
No state is required to complete the official count on election night. State laws set deadlines to certify final results, often weeks later.
Here’s a look at what could influence the timing of unofficial results.
Close margins
Polls and nonpartisan analysis show many U.S. Senate races are competitive, including in Michigan, Maine, Iowa, Alaska, Kansas and Texas. If the counts are close in the first few hours or even days after polls close, media outlets may have to wait for officials to count more ballots until journalists can project a winner. Some close races could end in a recount completed days or weeks later. In 2018, three Florida statewide races were settled in recounts.
Candidates who lead early in the vote count may not ultimately win. In 2020, Donald Trump was up by more than 100,000 votes in Wisconsin early in the night, but the picture quickly shifted after Milwaukee’s central count finished processing mail-in votes around 3:30 a.m local time. The late boost for Joe Biden from Milwaukee was expected, especially because Wisconsin’s mail-in ballots tend to skew Democratic.
The pattern of when votes are counted — and what political leanings those jurisdictions’ voters tend to have — varies by state.
Mail ballot volume and receipt deadlines
It takes time to process mail ballots. Election workers must verify voter identity, for example, by matching envelope signatures against registration records.
Most states, including Florida, require that mail ballots be received by Election Day. But some states allow voters to return ballots later as long as they were postmarked by Election Day.
In California, which runs nearly all-mail elections, ballots postmarked by Election Day and received up to a week later are permitted. The U.S. Supreme Court in June upheld the right of states to have such a policy, a blow to Trump, who says he wants a faster process and has spread falsehoods about California’s vote counting.
Ohio passed a law in 2025 that said most absentee ballots must be received by the close of polls on Election Day; previously it had a four-day grace period.
In California, counties must count and report the results from most ballots by the 13th day after the election. There are some exceptions to that, including for provisional ballots and mail ballots with signature verification needs; election officials should be done counting those within 30 days after the election.
In U.S. House races, there are always a handful of districts that are not called on election night or the day after, mostly in California, Lenski said.
Last minute absentee ballot submissions: A Michigan case study
When thousands of voters procrastinate sending in their mail ballots until the last minute, it takes election workers extra time to process and count those ballots. In past elections, some people have spread falsehoods about such “delays” in places like Detroit, pointing to vans with ballots arriving late at night as evidence of foul play.
The winner of the U.S. Senate race may not be clear until officials can count nearly all of Detroit’s ballots.
With more than a half million voters, Detroit election officials predict they will report results for approximately 95% of ballots on election night.
“It is an estimate, not a statutory deadline or guarantee,” said Daniel A. Baxter, Detroit elections chief of operations.
The variable is the number of absentee voter ballots received by 8 p.m. on Election Day (the deadline in Michigan law). Baxter said officials will make every reasonable effort to complete tabulation by 4 a.m., though it could take longer if a ton of absentee ballots arrive near the deadline.As of the evening of Oct. 26, about half of the 106,000 absent voter ballots in Detroit had been returned.
Detroit, a city that spans about 140 square miles, has 38 drop boxes. It takes a few hours after the polls close for election workers to collect ballots and bring them in a truck to Huntington Place for tabulation.
Smaller Michigan cities such as Troy, home to 66,000 voters, have a handful of drop boxes. During past elections, City Clerk M. Aileen Dickson said, Troy has finished counting ballots before midnight.
Preparing ballots for counting
No state posts mail ballot results before the polls close. But some allow election officials to begin processing mail ballots before Election Day. That means they can verify that the ballot was submitted by a valid voter, including checking signatures and often removing the ballot from the inner security envelope, flattening it and stacking it.
The steps election officials can take and when vary according to their state laws. A handful of states, including New Hampshire, don’t allow the process to begin until Election Day.
Ranked choice voting
Two states with competitive U.S. Senate races use ranked choice voting: Maine and Alaska. The system allows voters to rank their candidates in order of preference.
If a candidate wins more than 50% of first choices, then that ends the race. If not, the candidate who received the fewest votes is eliminated and voters who ranked that candidate first have their vote re-allocated to their second choice. That process repeats until a candidate wins over 50% of the vote.
Alaska accepts ballots mailed from outside the U.S. for 15 days after Election Day and has a long history of close races that take that long to count.
California races could take longer to count than Alaska this year, and any race recounts could run into December or beyond. A 2024 contested North Carolina state Supreme Court race did not lead to a resolution for about six months.
In Alaska, there are four Senate candidates on the ballot including Republican incumbent Sen. Dan S. Sullivan and Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., who will appear on the ballot without a party affiliation. In an unusual move, the U.S. Justice Department filed a lawsuit Oct. 22 seeking to block certification if the incumbent loses, alleging voter confusion. Lawyers on behalf of Mary Peltola, the Democrat, have asked the court to dismiss the case.
Maine could end up in ranked choice voting because Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic challenger Troy Jackson appear on the ballot along with six write-in candidates.
Municipalities report the results from the first round and then the state will know either the next day or the day after if it will proceed with ranked choice, Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows told PolitiFact. Historically, the state has known the ranked choice outcome the week after the election.
“We will work as expeditiously and efficiently as possible to get results as quickly as we can,” Bellows said, “but what is most important is that it is accurate and reflects the will of voters.”
This story was originally published on PolitiFact.com.
It is republished here as part of a reporting and fact-checking partnership between PolitiFact and Hearst Television.

title: Auto Loan Debt Is Rising Faster in Maine Than in Almost Every Other State
main_topic: Jobs, housing, and cost of living
text:
While everything seems more expensive in 2026, we have concrete numbers showing that auto loan debt is on the rise here in Maine.
👇 KEEP READING: 25 Maine Thrift Stores and Antique Shops Mainers Love 👇
WalletHub compared all 50 states using three metrics from its consumer debt data to measure changes in auto loan debt, average balances and monthly payments.
Each metric was graded on a 100-point scale and weighted to calculate an overall score used to rank the states.
Maine ranked second overall in WalletHub’s study of states where auto loan debt is increasing the most.
The state ranked third for its change in auto loan debt from the first to the second quarter of 2026 and 26th for its average auto loan balance and monthly payment in the second quarter.
According to the study, Maine’s average auto loan balance was $20,865, relatively low compared with most states, but it increased by more than 2.6% between the first and second quarters of 2026.
Residents paid an average of $523 per month toward their auto loans, and Maine ranked 27th nationally for its increase in auto loan delinquency.
And there you have it! Maine drivers carry a relatively modest average balance compared with much of the country, but that debt grew at one of the fastest rates in the nation during the second quarter.

title: Virginia GOP says shooting outside its offices in Richmond appears unrelated to its operations
text:
RICHMOND, Va. (AP) — The Republican Party of Virginia said a shooting Thursday just outside its offices in Richmond doesn’t appear to have anything to do with its operations.
The party said in a statement posted online that a woman was shot around 1:45 p.m. directly in front of the building that houses its offices.
Frank Loehr, chief financial officer for the Republican Party of Virginia, told reporters that he and other staffers were working inside the office when shots rang out outside.
A woman who had been speaking with two people who had a booth outside the building was brought inside the office bleeding after being shot, he said. The booth was not affiliated with the party.
The woman was conscious and moaning in pain, and it appeared she had been struck in the shoulder, Loehr said. First responders arrived quickly and took her away, he said.
“I was shook up, and I’m still a little shook up,” Loehr said.
The status of the woman is unclear. Police have not responded to phone messages, texts or emails.

title: 10-year-old girl found ‘tied up in a closet’ after being taken from apartment; suspect arrested, US Marshals say
text:
CANBY, Ore. (KPTV/Gray News) — A 10-year-old girl who was taken from her apartment early Wednesday was found that afternoon and a suspect was arrested, according to the U.S. Marshals Service.
The U.S. Marshals Service said tactical teams rescued the girl from a home in Oregon City, Oregon. She was found “tied up in a closet” and taken to the hospital.
Vince Edgar Chavez tried to run away out of the back of the house, but was arrested, according to the U.S. Marshals.
Investigators said a man went into an apartment at 1:39 a.m., hurt a 12-year-old child and took the 10-year-old. The 12-year-old was rushed to the hospital and was still being treated as of Wednesday afternoon.
Police said the parents are cooperating with the investigation.
The community asked why an Amber Alert was not issued when the girl was taken from her apartment, and the Canby Police Department said it had not gathered the information required for an alert.
Carus Elementary, where the girl is a student, had increased police presence during Wednesday’s afternoon dismissal “out of an abundance of caution.”
“Our hearts are with this child and her family,” the school district said. “Please know that we are here to support our students, staff and families in whatever ways we can.”

title: ‘He’s a monster’: Convicted Tennessee murderer still on the run as authorities investigate Wisconsin bank robbery
text:
LAKE COUNTY, Tenn. (WMC/Gray News) - The manhunt for escaped Tennessee inmate Jacob Allen Morley continues and authorities are investigating a possible link in Wisconsin after a man robbed a bank at gunpoint there on Tuesday.
Dane County authorities said the Bank of Deerfield was robbed just before it closed. A gunman walked in, demanded money, restrained two employees and left with cash. Nobody was hurt during the robbery.
The gunman stole a Lincoln MKZ from the parking lot to get away. The car was later found unoccupied.
The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation said it is aware of the robbery in Wisconsin, but has not confirmed it is linked to Morley.
Morley escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex Monday. He stole a white 2008 Ford F-150 marked with Lindamood Planting Company. The truck was found abandoned early Tuesday in Marion, Illinois. Police said there is no evidence Morley is still in that area.
Morley was serving a life sentence for the 2022 murder of Cody Birchfield.
Tyreece Miller, the U.S. marshal for the Western District of Tennessee, is asking for help in the search for Morley. The reward for information leading to his arrest is now at $15,000.
“He’s a monster. He will do it again,” Birchfield’s friend Daniel Russell said.
Morley is on the Tennessee Most Wanted List and should be considered dangerous.
Anyone with information about Morley is asked to call 1-800-TBI-FIND immediately. If you see him, do not approach him and call 911.

title: Here’s how much the Iran war has cost American taxpayers so far
text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The cost of the Iran war to American taxpayers has grown to $47.1 billion, according to a new estimate the Pentagon has provided to Congress. The fallout from the conflict has become a key issue in the midterm elections and could increase as President Donald Trump leaves open the possibility of renewed hostilities.
The figure from U.S. Central Command, which oversees operations in the Middle East, is as of Oct. 16 and offers the most up-to-date cost for the conflict since it was launched in late February by the United States and Israel. The latest price tag, obtained by The Associated Press this week, shows a $3.5 billion bump in U.S. spending since early September, when that figure stood at about $43.6 billion.
The growing cost of the unpopular war and its economic ripple effects on energy prices could hurt Republicans in next week’s midterm elections. Voters on Tuesday will decide which political party controls Congress during Trump’s last two years in office.
The Republican president has said new strikes on Iran are an option after the midterms and is sending more military resources to the Middle East, despite initially promising Americans a military campaign that would last only a matter of weeks. As the war’s costs in lives, tax dollars and economic impact grow, most voters say they want Congress to prioritize ending the conflict, according to a recent AP-NORC poll.
The expense of the conflict and military spending in general are already a contentious issue on Capitol Hill, where the Trump administration is pushing for the passage of a historic $1.5 trillion military budget proposal. The White House is also asking lawmakers to approve a $95 billion package that would help fund the Iran war and other priorities.
Wednesday marks eight months of the war, which Democrats have been trying to end through legislation that has failed to pass the Republican-controlled Congress.
“Trump and his ego led us into this war with no plan, no authority, and no exit strategy,” Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York said in a news release. ”Senate Democrats will continue to do everything in our power to end this disaster of a war and stop the costs, chaos, and corruption seeping from the White House.”
In the latest estimate, the bulk of the war’s costs are for replacing munitions, at about $29 billion. The advanced weapons most in demand and whose stockpiles have been drawn down are defensive missile interceptors, such as those launched by the Army’s Patriot and THAAD systems, with a single Patriot interceptor costing millions of dollars.
The Pentagon says about $11.9 billion is related to costs of operations, while an additional $6 billion is tied to equipment losses. The Air Force’s costs are now $7.6 billion, and the Army’s are more than $2 billion. The Navy’s costs were listed at $1.45 billion, which is a significant drop from the $2.2 billion listed in early September.
When asked why the Navy’s cost estimates decreased over the roughly six-week period, both the Navy and U.S. Central Command referred the questions to the Pentagon, which did not immediately respond to emails requesting comment on the new cost estimates.
The latest estimate does not include damage to U.S. bases in the Middle East, which the Islamic Republic has attacked with ballistic missiles and drones. A report from the Pentagon inspector general released last month said Iranian strikes have damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and other structures at U.S. bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan.
The Pentagon’s official tally lists 21 service members killed and 865 wounded in the conflict. That count includes troops who died in medical events and other situations that do not have a direct connection to the conflict, with 18 service members having been killed from Iranian strikes, combat aircraft crashes or the disposal of Iranian drones.
While Trump has mused repeatedly about whether to make a deal with Iran or “finish them off,” a third aircraft carrier and thousands of additional troops are making their way to the region. The Trump administration has also reduced staffing at some U.S. Embassies after receiving intelligence that Iran has stepped up efforts to target American personnel.

title: Man in wheelchair fatally struck by city-owned garbage truck, police say
text:
ROCHESTER, N.Y. (WHAM) — A man was struck and killed Tuesday by a city-owned and -operated garbage truck, and police are investigating.
Rochester police said they responded around 3:30 p.m. Tuesday to the city’s North Side and found a man dead at the scene.
What police say happened
Officers said a garbage truck was traveling eastbound on Warsaw Street and was attempting to make a left turn onto Hudson Avenue. At the same time, the man, who was operating a motorized wheelchair, was on the west shoulder of the road.
Witnesses said the wheelchair was pinned under the front end of the truck.
Police said the driver of the truck, a man in his 50s, was not hurt.
Officers do not believe drugs or alcohol played a role in the incident.
Bystander describes scene
Carl Canty came upon the scene minutes after the crash, as first responders worked to secure the area.
“You could see the wheelchair up under the garbage truck, and there were people that were there that were really pretty distraught at the situation in the scene,” Canty said.
Canty also said he feels for the driver of the truck.
“It was just kind of devastating to drive by and see that, and think someone just probably left, went to the store, wherever. They’re not going to return home,” he said.
City response
Rochester Mayor Malik Evans offered condolences and said the city is committed to conducting a thorough investigation to determine how the crash happened and what can be done to prevent further tragedies like this one.
The victim had not yet been identified.

title: Oscar-nominated actress Barbara Barrie dies via medical assistance, rep says
text:
Oscar-nominated actress Barbara Barrie dies via medical assistance, rep says
Oscar-nominated actress Barbara Barrie has died at the age of 95, her representatives confirmed to multiple media outlets.
Representatives on behalf of the Harnick family confirmed that Barrie's "passing was medically assisted in accordance with the New York State Medical Aid in Dying law, of which she was a proponent and advocate."
The New York Times said the "Suddenly Susan" actress had been diagnosed with terminal cancer and died at her New York City home on Oct. 28.
She had also previously disclosed a diagnosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a chronic, incurable lung disease, Playbill reported in September 2014.
During her career, Barrie made appearances across countless series, such as "Nurse Jackie" and "Law & Order: SVU."
Almost a decade before she was in contention for an Academy Award for her performance in 1979's "Breaking Away," the thespian earned a Tony nomination for her work in the original run of Stephen Sondheim's musical "Company."
E! News said Barrie worked for over 55 years in the industry after being introduced to acting at a community theater when she was around 11 years old.

title: Border Patrol agent charged with murder in wife’s death
text:
LAREDO, Texas (KGNS/Gray News) — A U.S. Border Patrol agent in Texas has been charged in connection with the death of his wife.
Abel Garza, 30, has been charged with murder, a first-degree felony, in the death of his wife, 28-year-old Mayra Alejandra Landeros, after a domestic disturbance in south Laredo.
U.S. Customs and Border Protection confirmed in a statement that Garza is a Border Patrol agent.
Garza also is charged with two counts of endangering a child and two counts of abandonment of a child. All four counts are second-degree felonies.
He was transported to Webb County Jail, and his bond was set at $1 million.
What police say happened
The incident happened just before 3 a.m. Wednesday at a home near Texana Street and Nocona Street.
Chief Miguel Rodriguez said police were initially called about a man knocking on doors asking for help. A police drone spotted a car leaving as officers arrived. Officers stopped the car and found Landeros in the back floorboard with critical stab wounds.
Landeros died later at the hospital. Her death marks Laredo’s sixth homicide of 2026.
Driver detained, children found safe
The 30-year-old driver, later identified as Garza, was detained. Police said the two were a couple. Officers found two children safe at the home.
“The person is in LPD custody, but they’re still in the process of formulating charges with the District Attorney’s Office guiding us,” Joe Baeza, of the Laredo Police Department, said.
CBP statement
In a statement, U.S. Customs and Border Protection said the man is an off-duty Laredo Sector agent who was arrested at 6 a.m. The agency said its Office of Professional Responsibility is reviewing the case.
